verdict.rationale: Missive documents its own rules engine: plans include 'Rules & automations' with up to 1000 rules. Rules can run multi-step over time, with each step checking conditions and acting on a conversation (for example, escalating unanswered emails at 24, 48 and 72 hours), and they can create drafts and run as AI rules. However, the evidence never spells out which events trigger a rule or the full list of available actions, so event-triggered coverage is only implied. Missing for 10: documented trigger event types (e.g., incoming message or assignment), a full action catalog, and independent or hands-on corroboration of rule behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote:
Automate your workflows

Up to 1000 rules
Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
Open a rule and click “Add a step” to get started. Delays can count calendar time or business hours.
Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server, now resolve {{ user.name }} and {{ user.email }} from your organization profile
